keys.statement: Choose an acid resin by its temperature limit: the review gives about 140 C for Amberlyst 15 and up to 190 C for Amberlyst 70. That limit bounds the temperature, and so the pressure, of a reactive zone.

plain.title: Acid resin catalyst: its temperature limit sets the reactive zone's temperature and pressure
plain.when: You choose an ion-exchange resin catalyst for esterification, for example in reactive distillation.
plain.do: Choose the resin by its maximum service temperature: about 140 C for Amberlyst 15 and up to 190 C for Amberlyst 70, per Hoff & Eisenacher 2025. Set the column pressure so the reactive zone stays below it.
plain.why: Resins lose their acid groups when too hot.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, check the reactive stages' temperatures against the resin's limit.

decisions.obstacle: Resins lose acid groups when too hot.
decisions.mechanism: Each resin has a maximum service temperature.
decisions.operation: Match the resin to the reactive-zone temperature.
decisions.expected_change: A catalyst that survives the column conditions.

keys.statement: Esterification is equilibrium-limited, so removing water continuously (reactive distillation, or a pervaporation or nanofiltration membrane in the reactor) raises conversion at milder conditions.

plain.title: Esterification at equilibrium: remove water continuously, by reactive distillation or a membrane
plain.do: Integrate water removal with the reaction: reactive distillation, or a pervaporation (membrane evaporation) or nanofiltration membrane in the reactor.
plain.why: Removing a product shifts the equilibrium, so conversion rises at milder conditions.
plain.check: Compare conversion with and without water removal in an equilibrium model.

decisions.mechanism: Removing a product shifts the equilibrium.
decisions.operation: Integrate water removal with the reaction.

keys.statement: For water-removal membranes, zeolite-coated ceramics (LTA or MFI type) withstand heat and chemicals better than polymer films. A polyvinyl alcohol membrane is reported to lose up to 35% of its permeability in 1000 h.

plain.title: Water-removal membrane in hot acid service: prefer zeolite-coated ceramic to polymer
plain.when: You choose a water-removal membrane for a hot reactive esterification mixture.
plain.do: Prefer zeolite-coated ceramic membranes (LTA or MFI type) to polymer films. Ceramic membranes can crack at large scale (Section 8.1).
plain.why: Inorganic supports resist swelling and chemical attack.
plain.check: Ask for long-term permeability data: a polyvinyl alcohol membrane is reported to lose up to 35% of its permeability in 1000 h.

decisions.obstacle: Membranes degrade in hot reactive media.
decisions.mechanism: Inorganic supports resist swelling and attack.
decisions.operation: Prefer ceramic zeolite membranes for hot organic acid service.
limits: Ceramic membranes are noted as prone to cracking at large scale (Section 8.1).

keys.statement: Homogeneous mineral-acid catalysts are active but corrode equipment, cannot be recovered and add purification steps. Solid acid catalysts avoid these drawbacks.

plain.title: Esterification catalyst: prefer a solid acid to a dissolved mineral acid
plain.when: You choose a catalyst for esterification.
plain.do: Prefer a solid acid catalyst where its temperature limit allows.
plain.why: A dissolved acid is active but corrodes equipment, cannot be recovered and stays in the product, adding purification steps. A solid catalyst stays in the reactor.
plain.check: Check the solid catalyst's temperature limit against the reaction temperature.

decisions.obstacle: A dissolved acid catalyst stays in the product.
decisions.mechanism: A solid catalyst stays in the reactor.
decisions.operation: Prefer a solid acid catalyst where its temperature limit allows.
decisions.expected_change: No acid removal step, less corrosion.

keys.statement: With water removed during the reaction, the review reports n-butyl acetate yields rising from about 70% to up to 95% using acidic ionic-liquid catalysts.

plain.title: Butyl acetate yield can rise from about 70% to 95% when water is removed during reaction
plain.when: Butyl acetate yield is limited by equilibrium.
plain.why: Water removal shifts the equilibrium towards the ester.
plain.check: Hoff & Eisenacher 2025 report this in one sentence from a cited study with acidic ionic-liquid catalysts, not read by Lab: treat it as an indication.

decisions.obstacle: Butyl acetate yield limited by equilibrium.
